topicName: Unreal Build Tool (UBT) and Unreal Automation Tool (UAT)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Unreal Build Tool (UBT) and Unreal Automation Tool (UAT)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unreal Engine provides two foundational command-line utilities that power the compilation, packaging, and deployment pipeline: Unreal Build Tool (UBT) and Unreal Automation Tool (UAT). Understanding how to leverage these tools is essential for setting up continuous integration (CI) and automating complex workflows."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Unreal Build Tool (UBT)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"UBT is a custom tool that orchestrates the compilation process of Unreal Engine C++ source code. It handles dependency tracking, target configuration, and platform-specific compilation parameters without relying heavily on native IDE project files."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parses module rules (.Build.cs) and target rules (.Target.cs) to map dependencies."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Generates platform-specific makefiles or solution files."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Optimizes incremental builds by analyzing header include graphs."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Invoking UBT from the Command Line"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"UBT is typically executed via the engine batch files. Below is an example command to build a target for a desktop project:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"Engine/Binaries/DotNET/UnrealBuildTool/UnrealBuildTool.exe MyGameTarget Win64 Development -Project=\"C:/Projects/MyGame/MyGame.uproject\" -WaitMutex"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Understanding Unreal Automation Tool (UAT)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"While UBT focuses exclusively on compilation, UAT is a higher-level automation framework written in C#. It orchestrates complex multi-step tasks such as cooking content, packaging builds, running automated tests, and deploying to mobile or console hardware."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BuildCookRun: The most common script combining compilation, asset cooking, and packaging."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"RunTests: Executes automated engine and project functional tests."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"BuildGraph: A powerful XML-driven dependency graph engine for advanced CI/CD pipelines."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Packaging a Project via UAT"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"To package your game for distribution using UAT, invoke the RunUAT script with the BuildCookRun automation script parameters:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"Engine/Build/BatchFiles/RunUAT.bat BuildCookRun -project=\"C:/Projects/MyGame/MyGame.uproject\" -noP4 -platform=Win64 -clientconfig=Shipping -serverconfig=Shipping -cook -allmaps -build -stage -pak -archive -archivedirectory=\"C:/PackedBuilds\""},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Integrating UBT and UAT in CI/CD Pipelines"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"When setting up continuous integration servers like Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions, UAT acts as the primary entry point. Because UAT internally calls UBT to handle source compilation, a single script can compile code, cook assets, and output a ready-to-test build artifact."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always pass the -unattended flag to prevent UAT from hanging on unexpected dialog boxes."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use the -stdout flag to pipe compilation errors directly into your CI console logs."},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"By mastering UBT and UAT command-line parameters, studio teams can completely automate their build releases, ensuring repeatable and reliable builds across all target platforms."}]
